A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DreamCS work, with matching authors, central methods, and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation experiments, human evaluations, reward-model generalization and robustness tests, and quality-versus-runtime ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation and human-evaluation results and adds scorer validation, mesh-fusion measurements, and comparisons involving additional generation methods.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix F.2 adds a reported adaptation that fine-tunes the TRELLIS generator using reward guidance, extending v2's per-asset SDS optimization procedure. The original RewardCS architecture, MSE-plus-CS training objective, differentiable meshization, adaptive mesh fusion, and progressive guidance remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds TRELLIS-500K-derived prompt/asset training data and a human-verified paired-mesh validation set. MVControl and DreamCraft3D experiments also introduce generated-image conditioning. These extend coverage within the existing 3D-asset domain; GPTEval3D, 3D-MeshPref, and the Recognize Anything-based tests remain.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 7–9 newly evaluate MVControl, ProlificDreamer, DreamCraft3D, and TRELLIS, including Reward3D and RewardCS variants of the latter three. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparison methods. The original comparator sets remain; DreamControl and MT3D are discussed but not actually benchmarked.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces ImageReward with CLIP under the retained 110-prompt, 12-view evaluation. New protocols include normalized Chamfer/95%-Hausdorff measurements across 40 prompts and five optimization checkpoints, plus additional generator comparisons using 30/60-prompt subsets and distinct stage budgets. These are added protocols, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of Llama-Mesh agreement with human preferences and geometric distortion from adaptive mesh fusion (Appendices B.2 and D.2). Conversely, v2 Appendix G.2's isosurface-resolution and guidance-frequency quality/runtime ablations disappear. Loss-weight, guidance-strength, generalization, and topology-robustness analyses remain; the t-SNE analysis is relocated, not new.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix E.2 first reports averaging three independent Llama-Mesh inference runs per mesh. v2 does not specify repeated annotation runs, so this establishes newly reported repetition and aggregation, not an increase from a known previous run count. Generation-result uncertainty remains unreported.

E6.justification: v3 adds CLIP results, 93.6% Llama-Mesh preference-ranking agreement, AMF measurements, and the comparisons in Tables 7–9, while removing v2 Tables 6–7's efficiency results. Table 1 changes MVDream+DreamDPO VR from -2.09 to -2.13, reversing its ordering against unchanged RewardCS (-2.11). Tables 2–5 retain their numerical entries; several prose values are corrected to match retained tables. IR and CLIP values are different metrics, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 2 corrects the CS overlap integral from p(x)p(y) dx dy to an integral of two densities over a shared variable. The asymptotic-equivalence theorem and proof remain substantively unchanged, with assumption references corrected. The new standard CD/HD formulas document evaluation metrics rather than introduce additional theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and main conclusion retain the same central claims: an unpaired 3D preference dataset, geometry-aware RewardCS learning, and DreamCS guidance improving geometric quality and human alignment. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the principal contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds a specific limitation concerning missing standardized Janus/multiview benchmarks, and explanations involving multistage 2D-reward instability and DreamCraft3D's DMTet compatibility. It also strengthens the argument for GA's evaluation fairness. v2's discussion of runtime costs, resolution tradeoffs, and overhead mitigation is removed.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses batch size 256, human rescoring for Llama-Mesh scores above 2.0, and settings/components for the added pipelines, including Stable Diffusion 3, Zero123-XL, and Omnidata. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments. It removes v2's main isosurface-resolution disclosure and public code/model release promise; core hardware and reward-training settings remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including MVControl, DreamControl, MT3D, DreamCraft3D, TRELLIS, CLIP, and Kwak et al. It positions controllable generation methods as dependent on conditioning or architectural assumptions and relates its annotation approach to prior automated pipelines with human verification. The core related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with local wording and numerical-prose corrections. v3 adds an appendix contents list, moves the LLM declaration into Section 6, separates annotation documentation and Janus discussion, and reorganizes the extended-results appendices. This is a limited restructuring rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds tables for AMF and expanded method comparisons and five TRELLIS multiview comparison figures, while removing the efficiency tables. It moves the existing t-SNE visualization into the main text, enlarges the framework diagram, and color-codes the main qualitative comparison. Most earlier qualitative panels are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 better substantiates previously asserted scoring reliability and mesh-fusion fidelity through Appendices B.2 and D.2, and Tables 7–9 strengthen evidence for broader applicability. Equation 2 and numerical-prose corrections also improve accuracy. These gains provide a limited net improvement: v2 already contained extensive empirical support, while v3 sacrifices useful runtime/quality analyses and meshing configuration information and leaves the TRELLIS fine-tuning objective underspecified.
